score_prompt: Create one original, exactly 120-second instrumental cinematic siege score for a future-dream cold open. An inhabited river city is already under aerial attack, and five fully grown, highly trained dragon guardians defend the last evacuation bridge. Score the danger seriously. From the first second the music must feel tense, urgent, muscular, and thrilling, never cozy, playful, whimsical, cute, or small. It is suitable for children because there are no horror shrieks, gore sounds, or jump scares, not because the music is softened. Use a driving 128 BPM pulse in 4/4: relentless low cello and bass ostinato, forceful nagara and taut tasha and pakhawaj strokes, low horns and trombones, urgent violas, and sparse high-string friction. The enemy has a descending three-note low-register figure. The guardians have an ascending five-note motif built from wide fourths and fifths; it must sound disciplined and battle-ready, never sing-song or triumphantly resolved. Preserve a clear center for dialogue, but keep the low pulse alive underneath speech. Leave brief openings for fire-breath, bridge-break, and shield-impact sound effects. Absolutely no pizzicato, santoor, bamboo-flute melody, ukulele, marimba, xylophone, glockenspiel, celesta, toy piano, handclaps, bouncy woodwinds, waltz, nursery-rhyme contour, comedy stingers, magic-sparkle music, choir, vocals, borrowed melody, electronic risers, or trailer braams. Begin in medias res at full siege tension. Preserve the siege pulse through every character reveal and repair. Build to an unresolved maximum-tension five-dragon launch at 01:53, then hard-stop without residue and leave 01:53-02:00 silent.
